title: Generative AI Toolkit - A Framework for Increasing the Quality of LLM-Based Applications over Their Whole Life Cycle
extended_summary:
This paper proposes the Generative AI Toolkit, a framework intended to improve the quality and reliability of LLM-based applications across their full development and operational life cycle. The authors frame the core problem as the manual, trial-and-error nature of current LLM application development, testing, deployment, and monitoring, especially given prompt sensitivity, hallucinations, and the need to maintain quality after release.

The toolkit is presented as an automation layer for DevOps-style workflows: it supports bootstrapping agents, defining custom metrics, creating repeatable evaluation cases, comparing model/prompt permutations, integrating testing into CI/CD pipelines, and logging/monitoring interactions at scale. The paper illustrates these features through example use cases such as a text-to-SQL agent, a restaurant menu RAG agent, an in-car assistant, and a model-comparison scenario. These are development examples rather than human-subject studies.

No K–12 population, teachers, or instructional coaches are studied. The main conclusion is that the toolkit can reduce cycle time, increase test coverage, and help surface quality problems such as hallucination, lack of tool use, or poor response quality, thereby improving development and deployment practices for LLM-based systems.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic large language model / generative AI application used to generate and evaluate text, prompts, and agent behaviors.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper presents a framework for developing, testing, deploying, and monitoring LLM-based applications and agents; the named examples are internal use cases and model comparisons rather than a specific educational product.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a framework/preprint about DevOps tooling for LLM-based applications, not an empirical study of an education AI tool. It does not report a controlled evaluation with participant outcomes relevant to K–12 teachers or coaches.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational impact outcome is measured. The paper discusses software-engineering benefits such as quality improvement and reduced cycle time, but provides no direct evidence of harm, null effect, or sustained teacher use in K–12 settings.
